AD_FIELD.NAME: Default Value
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. AD_FIELD.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Divide Rate By

AD_FIELD.HELP: To convert Source number to Target number, the Source is divided by the divide rate. If you enter a Divide Rate, the Multiply Rate will be automatically calculated.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Offset Month Due indicates the number of months from the current month to indicate an invoice is due. A 0 indicates the same month, a 1 the following month.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Fixed Due Date

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: SO Sub Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Sales Order Sub Type
AD_FIELD.HELP:
The SO Sub Type indicates the type of sales order this document refers to. This field only appears when the Document Base Type is Sales Order. The selection made here will determine which documents will be generated when an order is processed and which documents must be generated manually or in batches.
The following outlines this process.
SO Sub Type of Standard Order will generate just the Order document when the order is processed.
The Delivery Note, Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Warehouse Order will generate the Order and Delivery Note.
The Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Credit Order will generate the Order, Delivery Note and Invoice.
The Reciept must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of POS (Point of Sale) will generate all document

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Default Value
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Organization
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Organizational entity within client
AD_FIELD.HELP: An organization is a unit of your client or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Charge Amount
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The amount of a cost or expense incurred during business activity.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Charge Amount indicates the amount for an additional charge.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Order Reference
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A reference or document order number as listed in business partner application.
AD_FIELD.HELP: This can be used to input a reference for this specific transaction. For example, a Purchase Order number can be input on a Sales Order for easier reference.

AD_FIELD.HELP: Activities indicate tasks that are performed and used to utilize Activity based Costing

AD_FIELD.NAME: Partner Address
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Identifies the (ship from) address for this Business Partner
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Partner address indicates the location of a Business Partner

AD_FIELD.NAME: Project

AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifier of a project defined within the Project & Service Management module.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Processed
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A confirmation that the associated documents or requests are processed.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Processed checkbox indicates that a document has been processed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Date printed
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Date the document was printed.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the Date that a document was printed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Delivery Terms
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A definition stating when a specific delivery will occur.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Delivery Rule indicates when an order should be delivered. For example should the order be delivered when the entire order is complete, when a line is complete or as the products become available.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Freight Cost Rule
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The calculation method used when charging freight.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Freight Cost Rule indicates the method used when charging for freight.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Sales Transaction
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An indication that a transfer of goods and money between business partners is occurring.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Sales Transaction checkbox indicates if this item is a Sales Transaction.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Form of Payment
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The method used for payment of this transaction.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Form of Payment indicates the method of payment used for this transaction (eg. cash, wire transfer, etc.)

AD_FIELD.NAME: Print Discount
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An option to have any discount printed on the invoice.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Discount Printed Checkbox indicates if the discount will be printed on the document.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Tax
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The percentage of money requested by the government for this specified product or transaction.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Tax indicates the type of tax for this document line.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Accounting Date
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The date this transaction is recorded for in the general ledger.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The date this transaction is recorded on in the general ledger. This date also indicates which accounting period within the fiscal year this transaction will be part of.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Delivery Terms
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A definition stating when a specific delivery will occur.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Delivery Rule indicates when an order should be delivered. For example should the order be delivered when the entire order is complete, when a line is complete or as the products become available.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Delivery Method
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The desired means of getting requested goods to a business partner.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Delivery Via indicates how the products should be delivered. For example, will the order be picked up or shipped.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Default Logic 2
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Default value hierarchy, separated by ;
AD_FIELD.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Default Value
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Close Year
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: This proces creates the closing transactions and the corresponding opening transactions for the following year.
AD_FIELD.HELP: This proces creates the closing transactions and the corresponding opening transactions for the following year. The following year must already exist in the system and the first period must be open. The ledger accounting entries created by the Fiscal Year closing process are: 1. P&L Closing: Resets all revenue and costs accounts and posts P&L transaction. Currently posted into last day of last period of closing year. 2. Closing entry or Balance Sheet Closing: Creates closing transactions for asset and liabilities. Currently posted into last day of last period of closing year. 3. Opening entry: Posts opposite entry of closing entry. First day of first period of new year

AD_FIELD.NAME: Undo Close Year

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Document Status indicates the status of a document at this time. To change the status of a document, use one of the buttons usually located at the bottom of the document window.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Process Shipment
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Process Shipment (Update Inventory)
AD_FIELD.HELP: Process Shipment will move products out of inventory and mark line items as shipped.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Date printed
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Date the document was printed.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the Date that a document was printed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Charge Amount
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The amount of a cost or expense incurred during business activity.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Charge Amount indicates the amount for an additional charge.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Order Date
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The time listed on the order.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the Date an item was ordered.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Print
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A reference stating whether or not the document has been printed at any time in the past.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Printed checkbox indicates if this document or line will included when printing.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Client
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Client for this installation.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Accounting Date
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The date this transaction is recorded for in the general ledger.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The date this transaction is recorded on in the general ledger. This date also indicates which accounting period within the fiscal year this transaction will be part of.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Delivery Method
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The desired means of getting requested goods to a business partner.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Delivery Via indicates how the products should be delivered. For example, will the order be picked up or shipped.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Create Lines From
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An addition of statements from pre-existing documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A process that allows the user to copy lines (products) from an existing document different from the one being copied into. For example, in case of entering a new Goods Shipment, the user can copy lines (products) from an existing Sales Order or Sales Invoice.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Processed
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A confirmation that the associated documents or requests are processed.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Processed checkbox indicates that a document has been processed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Freight Amount
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The charge amount for a specified shipment.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Freight Amount indicates the amount charged for Freight in the document currency.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Movement Date
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The date that a certain item is moved from one location to another.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Movement Date indicates the date that a product moved in or out of inventory. This is the result of a shipment, receipt or inventory movement.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Freight Cost Rule
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The calculation method used when charging freight.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Freight Cost Rule indicates the method used when charging for freight.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Charge
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A cost or expense incurred during business activity.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Charge indicates a type of Charge (Handling, Shipping, Restocking)

AD_FIELD.NAME: Movement Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The type of a certain item being moved from one location to another.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Movement Type indicates the type of movement (in, out, to production, etc)

AD_FIELD.NAME: Posted
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An accounting status button that indicates if the transaction has already been posted to the general ledger or not.
AD_FIELD.HELP: An accounting status button that indicates if the transaction has already been posted to the general ledger or not. When doing the accounting manually this button can be used to post or unpost the transaction from the general ledger by hand.

AD_FIELD.NAME: User/Contact
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An acquaintance to reach for information related to the business partner.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The User identifies a unique user in the system. This could be an internal user or a business partner contact

AD_FIELD.NAME: Goods Receipt
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The document number for identifying an act of receiving goods.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Receipt ID indicates the unique document for this receipt.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Invoice
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A document listing products, quantities and prices, payment terms, etc.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Invoice ID uniquely identifies an Invoice Document.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Organization
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Organizational entity within client
AD_FIELD.HELP: An organization is a unit of your client or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Warehouse
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The location where products arrive to or are sent from.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Warehouse identifies a unique Warehouse where products are stored or Services are provided.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Process Shipment
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Process Shipment (Update Inventory)
AD_FIELD.HELP: Process Shipment will move products out of inventory and mark line items as shipped.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Business Partner
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Anyone who takes part in daily business operations by acting as a customer, employee, etc.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A Business Partner is anyone with whom you transact. This can include a customer, vendor, employee or any combination of these.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A value defining what sequence and process setup are used to handle this document.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Document Type determines document sequence and processing rules

AD_FIELD.NAME: Delivery Terms
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A definition stating when a specific delivery will occur.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Delivery Rule indicates when an order should be delivered. For example should the order be delivered when the entire order is complete, when a line is complete or as the products become available.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Sales Transaction
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An indication that a transfer of goods and money between business partners is occurring.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Sales Transaction checkbox indicates if this item is a Sales Transaction.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Order Reference
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A reference or document order number as listed in business partner application.
AD_FIELD.HELP: This can be used to input a reference for this specific transaction. For example, a Purchase Order number can be input on a Sales Order for easier reference.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Priority
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A defined level of importance or precedence.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Priority indicates the importance (high, medium, low) of this document

AD_FIELD.NAME: Description
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A space to write additional related information.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Partner Address
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Identifies the (ship from) address for this Business Partner
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Partner address indicates the location of a Business Partner

AD_FIELD.NAME: Purchase Order
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A unique and often automatically generated identifier for a purchase order.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Unique identifier and a reference to a Purchase Order originating from the document sequence defined for this document type.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Company Agent
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Purchase or Company Agent
AD_FIELD.HELP: Purchase agent for the document. Any Sales Rep must be a valid internal user.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Generate Invoice from Receipt
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Create and process Invoice from this receipt. The receipt should be correct and completed.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Generate Invoice from Receipt will create an invoice based on the selected receipt and match the invoice to that receipt.

AD_FIELD.NAME: 2nd Dimension
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A display of optional elements that are previously defined for this account combination.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The user defined element displays the optional elements that have been defined for this account combination.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Trx Organization
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The organization which performs or initiates the transaction.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The organization which performs or initiates this transaction (for another organization). The owning Organization may not be the transaction organization in a service bureau environment, with centralized services, and inter-organization transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Pick Date
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Date/Time when picked for Shipment
AD_FIELD.HELP: Date/Time when picked for Shipment

AD_FIELD.NAME: Tracking No
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Number to track the shipment
AD_FIELD.HELP: Number to track the shipment

AD_FIELD.NAME: Number of Packages
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The number of packages being shipped.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The number of packages being shipped.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Project
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Identifier of a project defined within the Project & Service Management module.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifier of a project defined within the Project & Service Management module.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Activity
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A distinct activity defined and used in activity based management.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Activities indicate tasks that are performed and used to utilize Activity based Costing

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An advertising effort aimed at increasing sales.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Campaign defines a unique marketing program. Projects can be associated with a pre defined Marketing Campaign. You can then report based on a specific Campaign.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Invoice Grouping
AD_FIELD.HELP:
For scheduled invoicing, break into different invoices if the related values are different. The value is used as a binary code with 15 digits: 1.-Order organization (AD_Org_ID) 2.-Order (C_Order_ID) 3.-Shipment (M_InOut_ID) 4.-Invoice location (BillTo_ID) 5.-Ship location (C_BPartner_Location_ID) 6.-Sales representative (SalesRep_ID) 7.-Payment rule (PaymentRule) 8.-Payment term (C_PaymentTerm_ID) 9.-Currency (C_Currency_ID) 10.-Campaign (C_Campaign_ID) 11.-Project (C_Project_ID) 12.-Activity (C_Activity_ID) 13.-Transaction organization (AD_OrgTrx_ID) 14.-User defined 1 (User1) 15.-User defined 2 (User2)
For example, if you want to create different invoices for each ship location for a customer, use the value "By ship location" (000010000000000)

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Process Work Requirement
AD_FIELD.HELP: By running this process the operations (activities) and products will be inserted automatically according to the selected process plan. Quantities will be multiplied according to the number of final products (Process Units) required. If the process plan selected does not have the "explodePhases" checked off, products from previously existing phases will be inserted only.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Validate Work Effort
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Process to validate and actualize stocks of all production runs.
AD_FIELD.HELP: With this process the work effort is closed. Stocks are actualized and average costs are calculated

AD_FIELD.NAME: Create Standards
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Inserts the standard values for the selected Work Requirement Phase and Cost Center version
AD_FIELD.HELP: With this process the products involved on the selected work requirement phase will be inserted. If the phase is of global use all the used products (P-) will go to the global use tab and if it is of no quantity all the quantities will be zero. This process also inserts the correspondent machines, salary categories and indirect costs of the selected Cost Center version. If the Activity of the Work Requirement Phase uses toolsets they are also inserted. Depending on the configuration of the Cost Center the process will also calculate the Cost Center use.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates a process plan.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

Process Quantity = Quantity x Conversion Rate

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Invoice Grouping
AD_FIELD.HELP:
For scheduled invoicing, break into different invoices if the related values are different. The value is used as a binary code with 15 digits: 1.-Order organization (AD_Org_ID) 2.-Order (C_Order_ID) 3.-Shipment (M_InOut_ID) 4.-Invoice location (BillTo_ID) 5.-Ship location (C_BPartner_Location_ID) 6.-Sales representative (SalesRep_ID) 7.-Payment rule (PaymentRule) 8.-Payment term (C_PaymentTerm_ID) 9.-Currency (C_Currency_ID) 10.-Campaign (C_Campaign_ID) 11.-Project (C_Project_ID) 12.-Activity (C_Activity_ID) 13.-Transaction organization (AD_OrgTrx_ID) 14.-User defined 1 (User1) 15.-User defined 2 (User2)
For example, if you want to create different invoices for each ship location for a customer, use the value "By ship location" (000010000000000)

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

Indicates whether the report is a "Point in Time" or a "Periodic" report.
A Point in Time report is obtained as of a given date, taking into account the whole historical financial movements; an example of point in time report is the Balance Sheet.
A periodic report is executed for a date range and it does not carry forward the balance of accounting movements previous to the range; an example of periodic report is the Income Statement.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Dependency Enforcement
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Dependency enforcement defines which are the versions of the dependent module that are compatible with the parent one.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Dependency enforcement defines which are the versions of the dependent module that are compatible with the parent one.
The values it can contain are:
*Major Version (default). The compatible versions are all the minor version within the same major version. If "Last Version" is defined being a different major version than "From Version", "Last Version" defines the highest compatible minor version; if "Last Version" is in the same major version than "From Version" this value is not taken into account. It is the default value. *Minor Version. Defines a strict dependency to the exact minor version. In case no "Last Version" is set, "From Version" is the only compatible version. Other case the compatible versions are all between "From" and "Last Version" values. *None. "From Version" is the only field taken into account, there is no restriction on different major versions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Instance Enforcement
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Instance specific dependency enforcement
AD_FIELD.HELP: In case the dependency is set as "User Editable", this value overwrites the Instance Enforcement one.

AD_FIELD.NAME: User Editable Enforcement
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Defines whether the enforcement can be overwritten by user
AD_FIELD.HELP: When a dependency/inclusion is "User Editable Enforcement", the enforcement defined for that dependency can be overwritten at instance level.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Name of the dependent module

It is the default value. *Minor Version. Defines a strict dependency to the exact minor version. In case no "Last Version" is set, "From Version" is the only compatible version. Other case the compatible versions are all between "From" and "Last Version" values. *None. "From Version" is the only field taken into account, there is no restriction on different major versions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Last Version
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Last compatible version
AD_FIELD.HELP: It is the last compatible version to define the dependency.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Instance Enforcement

AD_FIELD.HELP: In case the dependency is set as "User Editable", this value overwrites the Instance Enforcement one.

AD_FIELD.HELP: This is a secondary SQL where clause used by dbsourcemanager to filter data inside a table. This secondary whereclause needs to be written in SQL, and only applies for the dataset AD. When export.database is executed, this whereclause will be applied for the data inside the table, and only the records complying with it will be exported. The rest of the records (the ones which do not comply with the whereclause) will be ignored both in export.database and update.database. The main purpose of this whereclause is to select which of the records in a particular table are part of sourcedata, and which ones are part of client data.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Send Custom Queries to Heartbeat
AD_FIELD.HELP:
The Custom Queries are queries that can be sent by the Heartbeat server to be executed on the Openbravo ERP instance. This queries are used the get more extended information about the usage of the instance.
By disabling this option standard beats will be sent to HeartBeat server, but not these Custom Queries.
